patch.value: Recovery commands rendered on Windows are not paste-safe in PowerShell: $(...) and backticks expand inside CommandLineToArgvW double quotes

Recovery commands (`restore_with`, `suggested_retry`, next-step hints) are rendered by `quoteCommandArg` / `renderPmCommand` in `src/core/shared/command-line.ts`, used across 41 source files. On `win32` the helper follows CommandLineToArgvW quoting, which is correct for cmd.exe and CreateProcess, as settled in pm-b24b. PowerShell, however, expands `$var`, `$(...)` and backticks inside double quotes. An argument such as a tracker path `C:\trackers\$(Start-Process calc)` therefore expands when a user pastes the command into PowerShell. The argument comes from the user's own `--pm-path` or `PM_PATH`, so this is low risk, but recovery text should be paste-safe in the shell the agent actually uses.

CodeRabbit raised it on PR #1635 for `tests_omitted.restore_with`. It applies to every rendered recovery command, so it needs one shell-dialect decision instead of a per-call-site patch.

Decide the recovery-command shell dialect on win32 (cmd/CreateProcess, PowerShell, or a declared dialect field); quoteCommandArg renders arguments containing $, backtick, ( or ) so that pasting into the declared shell never expands them; unit tests cover win32 cmd and PowerShell rendering of a tracker path containing $(...) and a backtick; existing cmd/CreateProcess round-trip tests stay green
A recovery command rendered on Windows can be pasted into the declared shell without expanding $, $(...) or backticks in any argument.

value.text: Extension from the CodeRabbit review of PR 1681: the legacy intent restore_with renders its positional and the newly carried --fields with POSIX single quotes (shellQuote in src/sdk/context-intent-contracts.ts). On Windows cmd.exe, a retry such as "--fields 'id'" passes the quotes as part of the selector and fails validation. That recovery should use the platform-aware quoteCommandArg/renderPmCommand path this item owns.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Decision (2026-11-24): rendered pm commands follow a declared shell dialect instead of one fixed per-platform spelling. `resolveCommandShellDialect()` reads `PM_COMMAND_SHELL`: `posix` (aliases sh, bash, zsh), `cmd` (cmd.exe) or `powershell` (pwsh), case-insensitive. It defaults to `cmd` on Windows, which keeps the pm-b24b CommandLineToArgvW decision, and to `posix` elsewhere. An empty or unrecognized value keeps the default. The alias table is a Map, so `constructor` and other inherited keys never resolve.

Why not auto-detect: PSModulePath is set system-wide on Windows and inherited by cmd.exe children, so no environment signal reliably tells cmd.exe from PowerShell. No single spelling is safe in both shells either. `$(...)` is live in every PowerShell string form a cmd.exe line can carry, and `%VAR%` is live in every cmd.exe form a PowerShell literal carries. The failure direction picked the default. A cmd caret form pasted into PowerShell keeps its carets, so it names a nonexistent path and fails closed. A PowerShell literal pasted into cmd.exe expands `%VAR%` and can select another tracker.

PowerShell form: single-quoted literal with every quote doubled, including the typographic quotes PowerShell also accepts (U+2018/2019/201A/201B). The bare-token pattern quotes a leading `@` (splatting), `--` (parameter-binder token) and `,` (an array argument, which is joined with spaces for native commands).

Other call sites folded in: the legacy intent `restore_with` (POSIX `shellQuote`, comment 1 here) and the `git rm --cached` remediation in tracked-runtime-cache now go through `quoteCommandArg`. Credential redaction (`spanSpellings` in url-credentials) also registers the cmd caret spelling and the PowerShell doubled-quote spelling of each userinfo secret.

Proof: tests/integration/cli/rendered-command-shell-safety.integration.spec.ts runs a 22-argument hostile corpus through the real `sh -c`, `cmd.exe /d /s /c` (Windows native CI cohort, added to ci.yml) and `pwsh -EncodedCommand`. It asserts the program's argv byte for byte with a defined probe variable. Locally on Linux, POSIX passes, and PowerShell 7.7.0 (portable tarball) passes.

value.api: Rendered recovery commands (suggested_retry, restore_with, next steps) and the SDK quoteCommandArg / renderPmCommand
value.before: Windows recovery commands were always CommandLineToArgvW double-quoted, so PowerShell expanded $, $(...) and backticks; the intent restore_with and the git rm --cached remediation always used POSIX single quotes
value.after: PM_COMMAND_SHELL declares posix, cmd or powershell (default cmd on Windows, posix elsewhere); powershell renders single-quoted literals; every rendered command, including the intent restore_with and the git remediation, follows the declared dialect
value.migrate: Set PM_COMMAND_SHELL=powershell (or pwsh) when pasting pm recovery commands into PowerShell; SDK callers can pass a CommandShellDialect as the third argument of quoteCommandArg and renderPmCommand

message: Record defect escape class and gate evidence

patch.value: A recovery command rendered for the declared Windows shell can be pasted without expanding $, $(...), backticks or %VAR% in any argument

resolveCommandShellDialect reads PM_COMMAND_SHELL (posix/sh/bash/zsh, cmd/cmd.exe, powershell/pwsh; case-insensitive; Map lookup; unrecognized values keep the platform default of cmd on Windows and posix elsewhere). quotePowerShellCommandArg doubles every quote, including the typographic ones, and quotes a leading @, a bare -- and commas. quoteCommandArg and renderPmCommand take an optional dialect and are exported with the new quoters. The legacy intent restore_with and the git rm --cached remediation no longer hard-code POSIX quoting. URL-credential redaction registers the PowerShell, cmd caret and POSIX single-quote spellings plus their JSON-escaped forms, and reads cmd's %^40.

pwsh -EncodedCommand receives the 24-argument hostile corpus byte for byte with a defined probe variable (local pwsh 7.7.0); cmd.exe is proven by the Windows native cohort; unit tests pin cmd and PowerShell rendering of a tracker path containing $(...) and backticks; the CommandLineToArgvW round-trip tests stay green
Fixed in PR #1779: the recovery-command shell dialect is declared with PM_COMMAND_SHELL, and the powershell form renders single-quoted literals that never expand
